subject: Next steps: data processor scope, SOC 2 & vendor questionnaire
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@meditrust.com>, David Nguyen <david.nguyen@meditrust.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: data processor scope, SOC 2 & vendor questionnaire

Hi Sara / David —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned on compliance scope:

- Redwood readiness: we are SOC 2 Type II certified (report available) and we have a HIPAA-ready offering with BAAs. We also support GDPR data residency controls.
- What we need from MediTrust: primary security contact, list of data categories you expect us to process (PHI vs non-PHI), and any mandatory subprocessors you require us to disclose.

Actions I propose:
1) I’ll share our condensed security pack and a vendor questionnaire for you to review.
2) Sara — can you confirm if MediTrust needs us to include EU-based subprocessors specifically, or will an overall subprocessor list suffice?
3) If you’d like, we can start the vendor security questionnaire now and our Security team will return it within 5 business days for the sections requiring evidence.

Attachments: redwood-security-pack.pdf (summary), vendor-questionnaire.docx (fillable).

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
—
Redwood Inference | ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@meditrust.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, David Nguyen <david.nguyen@meditrust.com>
Cc: procurement@meditrust.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: data processor scope, SOC 2 & vendor questionnaire

Ben — thanks for the detailed recap. Helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- We are treating MediTrust as a HIPAA-covered entity for this engagement; any PHI processing requires a BAA and more stringent logging/audit evidence.
- EU residency: not required for the pilot, but we will need a clear list of subprocessors and data flow diagrams showing where tokens and PHI might cross regions.
- Primary contacts: me (security) and David (engineering). Procurement cc'd for contract routing.

I'll attach our initial intake spreadsheet to capture the scope: MediTrust-SQ-Initial.xlsx. Please fill the top-level questions and return; we will ingest it into our procurement flow.

Questions:
1) Can you provide your SOC 2 report or a SOC 2 summary (if redacted)?
2) Do you have a maintained subprocessor registry we can consume (CSV preferred)?

If you send the vendor questionnaire back, we can flag any high-priority evidence items up front.

Thanks —
Sara Kim
Security Program Manager
MediTrust Health

Mina — forwarding the MediTrust thread. They asked for: SOC 2 report or summary, CSV subprocessor registry, and confirmation about BAA for PHI.

Attachments included for your reference: vendor-questionnaire.docx (fillable). Can your team: 
1) Prepare a redacted SOC 2 summary and the subprocessor CSV slice for MediTrust.

Ben
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Next steps: data processor scope, SOC 2 & vendor questionnaire

Ben / team — noted. Plan and ETA below: 

Plan:
- SOC 2: We will prepare a redacted SOC 2 Type II cover letter + summary (no raw evidences). ETA: 1 business day.
- Subprocessor registry: I will export the current registry (CSV) and annotate columns for region and data purpose. This will include: AWS (us-west-2) - core inference + KV cache; GCP (europe-west1) - eval & analytics; Cloudflare - CDN/edge; Snowflake (us-east-1) - aggregated telemetry (no PHI).
- Vendor questionnaire: Security will complete the technical sections (A,B,C) and mark evidence items. Expect to return completed questionnaire + annotated subprocessor CSV.

Attachments I will provide: redwood-subprocessor-extract-20270511.csv and SOC2-summary-redacted-2026.pdf (SOC2-summary will be uploaded to the Drive link).

Constraints/notes: 
- PHI: we currently treat any PHI as isolated to customer-controlled encryption paths for dedicated/private deployments; for hosted pilot, we’ll include specific BAAs and retention terms in legal review.
- If MediTrust requires EU data residency for PHI we will need to engage Dedicated/Private options — that will affect pricing.

ETA: Completed package by EOD Friday (2027-05-14) if no unexpected items arise. If procurement needs a formal BAA sooner, loop Legal and I’ll prioritize.

Mina Haddad
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
